summary: East (Taylor) Fire Tower, a 1931 Aermotor in Osceola National Forest, NHLR-registered 2013; no dated source confirms it stands today.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor LS-4 tower with a 7x7 foot cab (NHLR)
facts.status_note: The NHLR lists the tower, but no dated source read confirms it stands today

access.note: Inside Osceola National Forest. No source read says the tower cab is open to climbers.

visit.trail_note: Osceola National Forest Road 202 (East Tower Trail) runs between CR 250 and CR 125 to a primitive hunting camp; onX recommends 4WD and high clearance.

events.note: Erected as a 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7x7 cab; formerly the Taylor Fire Tower; third lookout built on the Osceola National Forest

evidence.supports: Built 1931; formerly the Taylor Fire Tower; third lookout on the Osceola National Forest
evidence.quote: The East Fire Tower, formerly known as the Taylor Fire Tower, was the third lookout built on the Osceola National Forest.

evidence.supports: 100-foot Aermotor LS-4 tower with a 7x7 foot cab
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1931, it is a 100' Aermotor LS-4 tower with a 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: Erected in 1931 as a 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: 1931: A 100-foot Aermotor tower with 7'x7' cab erected.

evidence.supports: Forest Service historic archive photo titled Taylor Fire Tower 1931
Osceola NF Road 202 connects CR 250 and CR 125
evidence.quote: The East Tower Trail, also known as Osceola National Forest Road 202, connects CR 250 at the west end and CR 125 at the east end.

evidence.supports: The road gives access to the East Tower Camp, a primitive hunting camp
evidence.quote: gives you access to the East Tower Camp, a primitive hunting camp.

evidence.supports: 4WD and high clearance recommended on the road
Camp is a primitive camping area used mainly during general gun season
evidence.quote: This location is used primarily as a hunt camp during general gun season.

evidence.supports: Camp is described as a year-round primitive camping area
evidence.quote: Get back to nature while enjoying this year-round primitive camping area.

evidence.supports: NHLR location is Baker County, Florida
Photo sits in the Osceola National Forest Historic Archives collection on Flickr

corrections.why: The NHLR entry lists and describes the tower but does not say it stands today, and no dated source read confirms its current condition. The record should not assert standing without a dated source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR calls it the East Fire Tower, formerly the Taylor Fire Tower. The Eastern US lookouts page is titled East Tower (Taylor GS) and the Forest Service archive photo is titled Taylor Fire Tower 1931. These point to the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Current status is the main gap: no dated source read confirms the tower stands. Search snippets not read or cited: a Weebly listing line with a 1937 National Archives reference, and a social-media comment saying East Tower (Taylor) and Olustee Tower are different towers, which would be worth checking before any name merge. The Flickr photo has no image URL retrieved, so no photo entry was added. The onX page is a commercial trail guide, used only for road access.
